title: Taliban
capsule: The Taliban (طالبان) seized Kabul on 27 September 1996 after a rapid military campaign and declared the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, implementing a strict interpretation of Hanafi sharia combined with Pashtun tribal codes (Pashtunwali) under Supreme Leader Mullah Mohammad Omar. The regime banned women from education and employment, prohibited music, television, and photography, and destroyed pre-Islamic monuments including the Bamiyan Buddhas in March 2001. Following the September 11, 2001 attacks, a U.S.-led coalition invaded and the Taliban government collapsed by December 2001; the group resumed control of Afghanistan in August 2021 after the American withdrawal, making the 1996–2006 window in the dataset encompass both the first emirate and the early insurgency phase.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial control during 1996–2001 reached approximately 90% of Afghanistan but fluctuated with Northern Alliance holdouts; the post-2001 insurgency footprint is inherently difficult to map as bounded territory.
